claim: The medial C2 position may contain any single consonant or a cluster of up to three consonants; complex C2 clusters are restricted to specified structural classes rather than being freely combinatorial.

source_forms.C2: single consonant or cluster of up to three consonants

exceptions_or_counterexamples: The source separately identifies accidental gaps and rare/exceptional cluster realizations; cluster size alone does not imply all sequences of length <=3 are licit.

claim: A core medial-cluster class consists of homorganic nasal-stop sequences at the available places of articulation, including /mb, nd, nhdh, nydy, ngg/ and the retroflex nasal-plus-stop sequence represented as /rnd/.
formal_environment: N STOP between vowels within root
normalized_environment: Nasal+Stop medial cluster licensed when homorganic
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The retroflex sequence is discussed separately as potentially better treated as retroflex segments rather than an ordinary sonorant+apical cluster.

claim: Any consonant licensed root-finally can precede a bilabial or velar stop or nasal, or a bilabial/velar homorganic nasal-stop cluster, in medial C2 position.
formal_environment: {final-licensed sonorant} __ {labial/velar C or homorganic NC} within medial C2
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The source states these as structural possibilities and separately notes one accidental gap /yng/ among otherwise encountered combinations.

claim: Sonorant-plus-laminal medial clusters are much more sparsely attested than the peripheral-cluster class: Haviland lists /ldh, ydy, ynydy, ynhdh, ndy, ndh/ in roots, calls /ndh/ somewhat unusual, and reports /nhg/ as the only encountered case of lamino-dental /nh/ combining medially with another consonant.
normalized_environment: laminal continuations are restricted/low-attestation subset of otherwise predicted cluster space
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Haviland says such combinations seem possible in principle, so the finite attested list should not be recoded as a categorical exhaustive ban on all other sonorant+laminal sequences.

claim: Within the otherwise attested sonorant-plus-peripheral cluster possibilities, /yng/ had not been encountered and is explicitly described as presumably an accidental gap.
normalized_environment: Y+NG unattested in corpus but not grammaticalized as impossible
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The source explicitly rejects treating nonattestation as evidence for a categorical prohibition.

claim: Sonorant-plus-apical clusters do not occur as ordinary medial clusters. Apparent sequences written rd, rn and rnd are analyzed as retroflex stop, retroflex nasal, and retroflex homorganic nasal-stop respectively, preserving the generalization.

source_forms.analysis: retroflex segment(s), not ordinary sonorant+apical clusters

normalized_environment: *SONORANT+APICAL as medial cluster; retroflex representations are not counterexamples under source analysis
scope: language-wide medial cluster system as described
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The source notes these retroflex sounds can occasionally seem cluster-like phonetically, making the representational qualification essential.

time_scope: descriptive corpus collected before 1979; older versus younger Hopevale speech distinguished
claim: The root-internal medial-cluster restrictions extend across morpheme boundaries. Morphological operations such as reduplication can create illicit liquid-plus-apical sequences, which older speakers repair: /rr/ usually deletes before an apical, while /l/+apical undergoes retroflexization.
normalized_environment: repair(*LIQUID+APICAL): RR deletion or L-triggered retroflexization
scope: especially older-speaker speech; reduplication and suffixation
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Haviland notes rr deletion is not used by all Hopevale residents, and younger speakers frequently replace retroflex clusters with pronunciations such as gundaandal.

time_scope: descriptive corpus collected before 1979; speaker variation noted
claim: Non-nasal sonorants /y, w, l, rr, r/ do not occur as final members of ordinary root-medial clusters. Reduplication can create apparent violations with medial /w/, but such forms are rare and speakers commonly replace them with cluster-avoiding variants.
formal_environment: C __ {y,w,l,rr,r} as final member of medial cluster
normalized_environment: non-nasal SONORANT disallowed cluster-final medially; morphology may create rare corrected violations
scope: root-medial clusters; reduplicated forms as derived test cases
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Rare yiwarrwarr and baawawal violate the root pattern; speakers who use them often self-correct to the usual cluster-avoiding forms.
